ambiguity.description: It is unresolved whether the 0.4–1.2 mm power stubs violate the specified 2 mm minimum or are acceptable because inner-layer pours carry the bulk current.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: For VBUS and BAT−, which see the worst-case simultaneous current of up to ~3.2 A from 2.4 A charging plus ~0.8 A system load, I need confirmation on two points. First, do the F.Cu and In2.Cu pours remain contiguous from the USB-C or battery connector through to the AXP2101 VBUS and BAT pins, without any thin trace in series? Second, are there enough stitching vias between F.Cu and In2.Cu on those nets—typically 6+ vias for ~3.2 A? If both conditions are met, I am happy with the design. What concerns me is any 0.4 mm series bottleneck, since a 0.4 mm outer-layer trace carrying 3 A would run hot, with about a ~60 °C rise over ambient.

value_updates.worst_case_current_basis: 2.4 A charging plus approximately 0.8 A system load
value_updates.required_pour_continuity: Contiguous from the USB-C or battery connector through to the AXP2101 VBUS and BAT pins, with no thin trace in series
value_updates.stitching_via_expectation: Typically at least 6 vias between F.Cu and In2.Cu for approximately 3.2 A
value_updates.narrow_trace_acceptance_condition: Sub-2 mm stubs are acceptable only when they are not series bottlenecks and the contiguous copper pours carry the current

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: In that case, the design is acceptable and no further changes are needed for this issue.

routing_warnings.description: The observed absence of voltage at sensor pins concerns integrated-board power delivery behavior and does not specifically establish a high-current copper-routing failure.
The fluctuating L3 output is runtime evidence for DCDC1 regulation and load stability rather than high-current trace capacity.
The persistent failure after replacing AXP2101 belongs to the DCDC1 regulation trajectory and does not identify high-current routing as the cause.
